A_open.text: Thursday evening. Main Street. The Grove Cafe's sign says CLOSED. The lights inside say otherwise.
Georgia: PRIVATE TASTING. TONIGHT. 7. COME HUNGRY. BRING NOTHING EXCEPT YOUR OPINION.

A2_tasting.text: Chairs are up on the tables. Candles flicker. One table in the middle is set for a tasting.
Brad! You came! Georgia's been vibrating since noon.
She bribed me with a lifetime supply of black coffee. I'm weak.
In a corner booth, Professor Peters grades labs under a desk lamp. Thursday is her cafe night.
Welcome, welcome, welcome! First, the control group! My failed experiments, in order of regret!
Three plates: a Sardine Danish, a Pumpkin Tuna Melt, and something blue.
We don't talk about the blue one.

do.text: Brad takes a bite. He chews. He chews some more. His eyes water.
It's a pumpkin. And a tuna. Nobody asked them if they wanted to meet.
Respect.
Nobody's ever finished one before!
I'm saving my appetite for the star.
Coward.
Smart coward. The Surprise is much better.
I need to know about the blue one.
It was a blueberry situation. It's been in the fridge since September.
It has a name now. It's Gerald. We don't open the fridge.

A2_tasting.text: And now, behold! The Pumpkin Surprise!
A small tart sits on a plate. It glows faintly, like a very small, very edible lighthouse.
Georgia. Is it supposed to glow?
It's pumpkin from Gord's special crop. The back patch. He only sells those to me.
Dad sold you Patch Seven pumpkins? He's never sold those to anyone.
I asked nicely. And I brought pie.

then.text: Also, a dash of the lab foam. A tiny dash! For science!

A2_tasting.text: Brad, you're the guest of honor. First bite is yours.

B_bite.text: Brad takes a bite. The tart is warm, sweet, and a little tingly. It tastes like autumn.
It's good! It's really...
Brad's smile freezes. His eyes widen. He sets down his fork.
I'm terrified I'm going to fail my father's legacy.
Everyone here knows who he was. I don't. What if I'm not him? What if I'm just me?
The cafe goes silent. A candle pops.
Oh, Brad.
...Same. About the tavern.
Why did I say that out loud?
That's the pumpkins. It's not the dessert. It's the pumpkins.
One by one the others take a bite. Each goes very still.
I salted Dad's coffee on purpose. Twice. He didn't notice.
I cry at dog food commercials. Never when anyone's looking. Always when nobody is.
I put anchovy in the muffin because I lost a bet to my brother!
Four people around a glowing tart, laughing, wincing, and telling the truth.
It is the most honest dinner party in Ravenwood history.
I noticed in August. Dale ate a muffin. He quit his job and told his mother he loves his barber.
Then he napped.

then.text: The cookie! The meatloaf! That was this!
I'm so sorry! I thought you'd forget!

B_bite.text: It lasts about thirty minutes. Then you go back to normal. But everyone remembers.
So the pumpkins make people honest. Because of the soil?
The glow. The hum. Dad's secret. Is this what he's hiding?
In the corner booth, Patricia has stopped grading. She is staring at the tart's glow.
Ms. Grove. Where exactly did those pumpkins come from?
Gord's back patch. Number seven!
...I see.

then.text: Good evening, everyone. Do not eat any more of that. Especially in public.
Patricia gathers her papers and leaves so fast she forgets her tea.

else.text: I'll stay. For purposes of... observation.

B_bite.text: The group drifts apart in the candlelight. Brad finds himself alone with one person.

C_j.text: Jane sits at a window table with a thermos and a study guide. The tart glows beside her.
What's the powerhouse of the cell?
A pumpkin. Honestly? I haven't studied. I've watched you carry things badly since day one.
It's my favorite part of the week.
I can't stop. Also, I'm worried about Dad. He's hiding something about the pumpkins.
And I'm tired of being the responsible one. I want dessert for dinner. And to dance badly.
It's the tart. For thirty minutes, you can't lie.
...Then ask me anything. I can't stop myself.

C_j.prompt: Jane has no filter. Brad has a choice.

do.text: What exactly is your dad hiding?
He goes out to Patch Seven at night with a lantern. And talks to it.
There's a padlocked shed by the back field. I don't have the key. I've tried six times.
...I wish you hadn't asked. I couldn't say no.

options.text: You don't have to carry it alone

do.text: You don't have to carry it alone. Whatever's going on, we'll find out together.
...I didn't know I needed someone to say that.
Thank you. For not using it against me.

C_j.text: They sit in silence, watching the candle burn down while the glow on the tart fades.

C_s.text: Sandra sits at the counter with a paper cup of black coffee. Her tart glows, half eaten.
I'm going to say things now. It's unavoidable. Do not write them down.
You're the only person who doesn't flinch at my face. I assume it's a medical condition.
Your face is fine. It's the lipstick that's intimidating.
That's... the nicest thing anyone's said about my lipstick.
She freezes. The coffee cup crumples in her fist. Coffee drips onto the counter.
That was not supposed to come out. That is a thing I think. Silently. In my head.

C_s.prompt: Sandra stares at the ruined cup, not at Brad.

do.text: You like having me around? Really? Say it again!
No. It was a coffee-induced hallucination.
Please don't make me regret this.
I like having you around too.
...Fine. That was less terrible than I feared.
We're both being honest. Don't ruin it.
So. Tavern trivia night. Do you win a lot?
...Thank you. I always win. Ask me about the rules and I'll talk for an hour.
Sandra talks about trivia night for ten minutes. She glows, and not only because of the tart.

C_s.text: Tavern closes soon. I'll walk you out. Not because it's late. Because I like the walk.

C_g.text: The others have gone. Georgia stands behind the counter, polishing the same spot on the same cup.
From under the register she takes a crumpled envelope.
Pastry school application. I keep it next to the tip jar. Where I can't see it, but I know it's there.
I'm afraid I'll be the cafe girl forever. I want to bake in a city. A tiny bakery on a big street.
I never sent it. My family needs me. Everyone needs me. Nobody asks what I need.

C_g.prompt: Georgia is telling the truth. All of it.

do.text: Georgia. Do you... like me? Like me, like me?
Yes. Obviously. Since the cookie.
...You asked while I couldn't lie. That's not fair.
You deserve to ask for what you want. Send the application.
You asked what I need. Nobody does that. Thank you.
She presses the envelope into his hand. 'Hold this for me. Until I'm brave enough.'
You can't leave. Who'd put anchovy in the muffins?
Ha! Nobody else has the courage!
Thanks. I needed to laugh more than I needed advice.

C_g.text: Georgia blows out a candle. Then another. The glow on the tart is fading.

C_p.text: In the corner booth, Patricia has abandoned her grading and studies the tart with suspicion.
One bite. For the sake of science.
She takes a bite. She sets down her fork very carefully.
I blame ravens for everything because the alternative is that I'm responsible.
I haven't slept since Wednesday. The lab was my mother's. I am afraid of it.
Your father was my mother's best student. She loved him like a son.
I'm lonely at faculty parties. There. Nobody tell.
Mr. Bart. Whatever I say for the next half hour. Please. Be kind.

do.text: What happened to the program?
My mother never told me. But she stopped serving punch at faculty parties. For life.
Whatever happened, it involved a dance, and a punch bowl, and something she regretted.
...You asked while I couldn't refuse. I won't forget that.
Tell me your favorite lab disaster. I'm told there are many.
You... didn't ask. You gave me the room to keep it. Thank you.
The best was a Bunsen burner, a banana, and a very ambitious sophomore.

C_p.text: Mr. Bart. I'll walk myself to my car. Strictly because it's dark. Not as a date.

D_close.text: Thirty minutes later the glow fades. The candles burn low. Nobody quite looks at anybody.
I said nothing. Nobody said anything. The tart is a liar.
Thank you all for coming to the tasting! Please leave a kind review!

then.text: Brad. Next time, if I can't say no, you shouldn't ask. Okay?
Please forget what I said. We'll both pretend.

else.text: Mr. Bart. I'd appreciate it if tonight went unmentioned in class.

D_close.text: Everyone agrees not to ask why the pumpkins did that.
A tap at the window. The crow, outside in the dark, taps the glass twice.
Brad walks the farm road home. A lantern glows on the porch. Gord sits rocking, not looking up.
She's the only one I sold the back-patch pumpkins to. I regret it a little more each day.

D_close.prompt: Gord stares into the dark field.

options.text: Tell him what the tart did

do.text: People told the truth. All of them. For about thirty minutes.
Thirty. It was ten, in my day.
In your day?
...Never mind. Bed.
Uncle Gord. What's in Patch Seven?
Not tonight.
...Soon. Not tonight.
Goodnight, Uncle Gord.
Night, boy.

D_close.text: Saturday. Six. Bring your boots. We're doing the pumpkins.
In the far field, something glows faintly orange. The crow lands on the porch railing and watches.
